clue.text: Sybil's consort, as viewed I see before a church

parts.note: Sybil Fawlty's husband in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers is Basil
the phrase 'I see' as it looks written in letters: I and C (the letter that sounds like 'see')

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about the husband of a woman named Sybil, glimpsed standing in front of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s British sitcom; Basil Fawlty runs the hotel with his wife Sybil. 'before' just puts the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, especially one given special privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: Run for cover? Hardly!

parts.note: a dash with no cover at all: running naked across a public place, the opposite of seeking cover

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run for cover' suggests fleeing to shelter; 'Hardly!' turns it round into a run without any covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, a run with no clothing to cover the runner.

clue.text: But he had no quarrel with Beaumont, apparently

definitions.text: But he had no quarrel with Beaumont, apparently

parts.words: But he had no quarrel with Beaumont, apparently
parts.note: the Jacobean dramatist who wrote plays jointly with Francis Beaumont; his surname is a trade that makes arrows, and a quarrel is a crossbow bolt

explanation.walkthrough: A quarrel is a square-headed crossbow bolt; the arrow-maker 'had no quarrel' only in the sense of a row, since he worked happily with his co-author.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher co-wrote plays with Francis Beaumont, and a fletcher by trade is an arrow-maker, so one might expect quarrels about him.

clue.text: Shark found in American rivers

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A predatory fish turns up in the waterways of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'rivers' supplies two pieces: a named river, the Ure, and the abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark is a moneylender charging extortionate interest, which is exactly what a usurer is.

clue.text: Tartan cape putting one in shade

indicators.note: 'putting one in' tells us to place the numeral inside the name of the cape

parts.note: Cape Wrath is the headland at the north-west tip of Scotland, so a Scottish (tartan) cape
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone drapes a tartan cloak over a figure standing in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tartan' is not plaid cloth here but a jocular word for Scottish, pointing to Cape Wrath.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost or spirit, and a wraith is likewise a ghostly apparition.

clue.text: Why, as Hitler might have said, deface the old republic?

indicators.note: a German speaker pronounces W like V, so the English word is said with a German accent

parts.note: said in a German accent the word sounds like the first syllable of the city's name
to mar is to spoil or deface

explanation.surface: A question about why the dictator wished to disfigure the former German state.
explanation.walkthrough: German W sounds like English V, so the city's name sounds like 'Why mar' in a German accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weimar Republic was the German state from 1919 to 1933, named after the city where its constitution was drawn up.

clue.text: State line question dividing temperance movement

indicators.note: the pieces split the two letters of the movement apart, sitting between them

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is the movement for people giving up drink
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: A border dispute splits a group of teetotal campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: Alaska became a US state in 1959.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Beau ideal falling in love during the commercials

indicators.note: the zero and the turned word come during the commercials, inside them

parts.note: ads are television commercials
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word falling is read from bottom to top, so the word 'in' is turned round

parts.note: the word is taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: A handsome man falls in love while the adverts are on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling' turns 'in' upside down, which works because this is a down clue; 'during' puts that and the love-zero inside the adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name means a model of male beauty, a beau ideal.

clue.text: "Is this my farewell party?": FAQ during one's execution

indicators.note: carrying out a performance of letters, the fodder is executed into a new order

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A condemned man asks whether his goodbye gathering is a celebration, and someone hands him a list of frequently asked questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution' signals rearranging FAQ, DURING and IS; the definition plays on the group as a 'party' that sees someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A firing squad is a group of soldiers who shoot a condemned person, jokingly a party for the final farewell.

clue.text: Vote Democrat, I see

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: A voter announces they back the Democrats and understands the choice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament, members divide to vote, walking into separate lobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: In the House of Commons a vote is held by a division, so to divide is to vote.

clue.text: Combined forces around Nile port

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Allied armies gather near a harbour on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation, a combination of police forces from many countries.

clue.text: Dried flower bed with a deep irrigation from the roots

indicators.note: the roots of words are their starts, so the first letter of each is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to water a parched garden bed deeply so the moisture reaches the plants' roots.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, a river, so its bed is a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a valley or watercourse in desert regions that is dry except in the rainy season, a dried riverbed.

clue.text: Labour creator, bitter one in Ireland after work finishes

indicators.note: the rest of the answer comes after that letter
the finish of the word 'work' is its last letter
the harsh word and the numeral go inside the name of the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
hard means harsh or bitter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bitter Irishman, once his job is done, founds the Labour movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Hardie (1856-1915) was a Scottish founder of the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Hardie was a founder and first parliamentary leader of the British Labour Party, so one of its creators.

clue.text: Decent property cages raving maniac

indicators.note: a maniac behaves wildly, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A respectable house is home to a lunatic who rattles the bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' means a quality someone has, not real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving grace is a redeeming quality that makes up for faults, a decent property in a person.

clue.text: Pope freed by Inquisition?

definitions.meaning: one declared not guilty and released by inquisitors

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense is a playful reading: someone the Inquisition found blameless.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent is a papal name, and someone found guiltless and set free by an inquiry is innocent.

clue.text: Church put a resolution about introduction of Zionist brass

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the first letter of Zionist
resolving these letters means working them out into a new order

parts.note: the words 'put a' as printed, plus an H the setter seems to have meant to include, so the anagram has the five letters it needs

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A church passes a motion on admitting a Zionist leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder 'put a' lacks the final H; 'resolution' rearranges it and 'about' wraps it round Z, 'introduction of' Zionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass in British slang means cheek or impudence, which is what chutzpah means.

clue.text: "Who-dun-it?", she asked. "Saint Henry of Uluru?"

parts.note: Uluru was long called Ayers Rock, named after Sir Henry Ayers

explanation.surface: A woman asks who committed the crime, then wonders whether a saint lives at the great Australian rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Uluru, the great red rock in central Australia, was named Ayers Rock after Sir Henry Ayers, a premier of South Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels, each posing the question of who committed the crime.

clue.text: The foreign soldiers retreating without a gong from their field marshal?

indicators.note: without means outside: the reversed pieces go outside the medal
the soldiers going back means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
the MM, Military Medal, is a gong or decoration

explanation.surface: Enemy troops in retreat, with no medals, flee from their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; the question mark is there because Rommel commanded German forces, the 'foreign soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erwin Rommel was a German field marshal, so the commander of the foreign soldiers.

clue.text: Can one cleave the brand in the Caribbean?

indicators.note: to cleave is to split, so the can and numeral split the brand open

parts.note: a marque is a brand, especially of cars
a tin is a can
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question whether a single tin can be split by a cocktail label on a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb opening a question; it is a noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French island in the Lesser Antilles, so it lies in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Tin provided that female inside with lunch

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for the can

parts.note: if means provided that

explanation.surface: A woman is shut inside a tin box along with a packed lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin, from British India, is a light meal taken at midday, that is a lunch.

clue.text: See old rock topped

parts.note: ex- means former or old

indicators.note: topping removes the first letter

parts.note: Peter means rock, from Christ's words to Simon Peter

explanation.surface: A look at an ancient rock with its summit cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a bishop's diocese; Exeter is a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese of a bishop, and Exeter is the seat of one.

clue.text: Saucers suspended, some say, without handles

definitions.text: Saucers suspended, some say, without handles

parts.words: Saucers suspended, some say, without handles
parts.note: flying saucers said to hover in the sky, a handle being a name, so these are unnamed or unidentified

explanation.walkthrough: 'without handles' suggests crockery with no grips; a handle is slang for a name, hence unidentified flying objects.
explanation.definitionFit: UFOs are unidentified flying objects, popularly flying saucers, whose existence some people claim.

clue.text: Cruel fate trapping colt by first bet

indicators.note: the preposition comes first in the answer

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: the rearranged word traps the colt's letter inside it
cruel treatment mangles the word into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for colt in racing form

explanation.surface: A harsh destiny catches a young horse after its first wager.
explanation.walkthrough: A perfecta (called an exacta in some places) is an American bet; 'Cruel' scrambles only 'fate', and 'first' puts the preposition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfecta is an American bet picking the first two finishers of a race in the correct order.

clue.text: Catalytic converter's frenzy, methane emitted

indicators.note: the letters are given off from inside the words, sitting across the two of them

explanation.surface: A car's exhaust device goes wild, belching out gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catalytic converter' sounds like car parts, but it is a literal description: a thing that converts by catalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that acts as a biological catalyst, speeding up the conversion of substances.

clue.text: Stylish women quitting sewing circle abroad

indicators.note: abroad means all over the place, so the letters are scattered
the women leave the word, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Women walk out of a needlework group in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quitting' takes W out of SEWING, leaving SEING; with O, 'abroad' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Soigné is French for well groomed and elegant, so a synonym of stylish.

clue.text: Flog on the butt

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the butt is the hind end or tail

explanation.surface: An order to beat someone on the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like whipping but is the slang sense, to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is British slang for sell, and to retail is to sell goods to the public.
